frame: candidate minus the Modern Bhāratīya (dṛk) tier in the tropical frame (each candidate with its own ayanāṃśa); the ayanāṃśa column is candidate minus Citrā-pakṣa

measured.fittedOn: 1850-2150, every 97 days (1130 samples): the whole span the dṛk tier serves; the 2026, 1900-2100 and 1862-2138 spans lie inside it
measured.method: least squares of the Kerala tier's tropical residual against the dṛk tier on a constant plus the terms; the constant (the ayanāṃśa's business) is not applied

dvitiya.provenance: Munjāla, Laghumānasa c. 930 CE — the first attested Indian second inequality (the owner's Moon dossier §3, after Duke); not in this library's editions [paramparā, unverified here]; the argument is the evection's

variation.provenance: no Indian source (Tycho) — the owner's Moon dossier §3 [standard]

annual.provenance: no Indian source (al-Zarqālluh, Tycho) — the owner's Moon dossier §3 [standard]

sunManda.form: × the Sun's own manda-phala (a scale on the 14° epicycle)

moonManda2.provenance: the second harmonic of the equation of centre (the ellipse's e² term, 0.214° in the sky) — no Indian source; the epicycle cannot give it [standard form, measured amplitude]

reduction.provenance: the reduction of the orbit's longitude to the ecliptic (−0.114° sin 2F in the sky) — no Indian source [standard form, measured amplitude]

moonD.provenance: the parallactic inequality (−0.035° sin D in the sky) — no Indian source [standard form, measured amplitude]

drikTrueNode.unit: arcminutes (mean, rms, max) of (true node − mean node) − series; amplitudes in degrees, on the tier's own mean angles D = L_M − L_E, g = L_M − P_M, g′ = L_E − P_E, F = L_M − N_M

planets.unit: arcminutes (mean, rms, max); epoch in degrees, rate in degrees per Julian century; scales and radial terms dimensionless; manda2 and the series in degrees
planets.method: Levenberg–Marquardt on the dṛk residual through ss-tier planetWithBija, in two forms per graha, staged — the text's four steps: the mean and śīghrocca bīja (4), + the mandocca bīja (6), + the two epicycle scales (8), + the second manda harmonic (9), + the radial variation (11); Nīlakaṇṭha's placement: the bīja (6), + the śīghra scale and the first series term (8), + the series (10), + the radial variation (13); the better form kept per graha (`form`)

meanSunCentre.note: the text's own centre of the śīghra (TS 2.70, 2.73-74: the mean Sun) with the same measured series and radial terms; the tier uses the true Sun, which measures better — this is what Nīlakaṇṭha's form itself achieves with measured amplitudes

eclipses.generatedBy: scripts/measure-eclipses.cjs (the text's shadow and the chapter-5 parallax measured against the dṛk tier's eclipses at Ujjain)

shadow.method: the Kerala default's lunar magnitude (SS 4.10-4.11 on the measured places) against the dṛk umbral magnitude at the eclipses both list (middles within 0.1 d); channa = (moon + shadow·(1 + s))/2 − |β| is linear in s at the middle, so s is the closed-form least-squares scale on every other matched eclipse (even index), the odd ones held out
shadow.unit: magnitude (the covered part ÷ the Moon's disc); scale dimensionless on the text's tamas (4.4-4.5)

parallax.method: at every new moon of the span where either tier has a solar eclipse at Ujjain, the Kerala model's covered fraction (samskara.js solarOnModel: channa ÷ grahya, clipped at 0) against the dṛk tier's local magnitude (0 where the site is outside the eclipse); the text's nati (5.10-5.12) × (1 + natiScale) and the middle's lambana (5.8-5.9) × (1 + lambanaScale) chosen on a grid (0.1, then 0.02 and 0.005 about the best) to minimise the mean square on every other event, the rest held out
parallax.unit: magnitude (the covered part ÷ the Sun's disc); scales dimensionless on the text's nati and lambana

eclipses.note: measured on the Kerala default's places without these scales (what is measured is the bare shadow and parallax); the joint candidates carry the three amplitudes (ss-tier measuredFromRecord); the validation (scripts/validate-oos.cjs) re-counts the eclipses with them applied

candidates.par+ayanPhase: + Parameśvara's 15° as a phase shift alone (the morning's default of 2026-10-09; it breaks Āryabhaṭa's zero by 57.6′: superseded)
candidates.par+ayanAmp: + the same single record as an amplitude change alone (within a minute of the three-record fit)
candidates.par+ayan3: + the libration fitted to the paramparā's three determinations — Āryabhaṭa's zero in Kali 3600, Nīlakaṇṭha's 14°26′, Parameśvara's 15° — on its phase and greatest value: THE DEFAULT TIER (adopted; residuals 0, −0.5, +0.5′)
candidates.par+keralaLin: + Nīlakaṇṭha's stated linear rule (14°26′ + 0.9′ a year) instead: it misses Āryabhaṭa's zero by 56′, kept as a cross-check
candidates.par+keralaLin+sunEpoch: + Parameśvara's epoch Sun as a shift of the text's (a canon difference, not a correction: not adopted)
candidates.kerala: the Kerala tier: Parahita + Dṛggaṇita means, the text's epicycles, the line through the three determinations
candidates.kerala+vakyaMoon: the same with the Moon of candravakya.js (Mādhava's sine, the 31.5 epicycle [unverified])
candidates.kerala+dvitiya: the Kerala tier + Munjāla's second correction (the evection's argument), amplitude measured [paramparā form, measured amplitude]
candidates.kerala+dvitiya+var: + the variation (no Indian source) [standard form, measured amplitude]
candidates.kerala+dvitiya+var+annual: + the annual equation (no Indian source) [standard form, measured amplitude]
candidates.kerala+manda: the Kerala tier with a measured scale on each of the text's manda epicycles (14° Sun, 32° Moon) [measured]
candidates.kerala+all: all five measured forms together — what the sibling Kerala-corrections file (SSEA / sphuta / web) would do here, with every amplitude fitted, none typed [measured]
candidates.kerala+all+bija: the joint measurement: a bīja (epoch + rate) on the Sun's, the Moon's, the apogees' and the node's means, the five forms, the Moon's second manda harmonic and the reduction to the ecliptic, and the five planets with bīja, epicycle scales and second harmonic — all fitted through the tier's own arithmetic [paramparā and standard forms, every number measured]
